unit-ww501-syn.title: Wordly Wise · Lesson 1 Synonyms & Antonyms
unit-ww501-syn.source: Vocabulary Unit 1: Synonyms and Antonyms — Wordly Wise Lesson 1 study sheet (Drive)

summary.text: The class study sheet for Lesson 1, built around one synonym and one antonym for each of the 15 vocabulary words — the same list unit-ww501 already covers, tested a different way. The sheet itself says the unit test draws directly from these pairs.

why.text: A synonym or antonym is really a small proof that you understand a word's meaning, not just its spelling — you have to know what "accustom" means before you can spot "ignore" as its opposite. That is exactly the kind of recall a unit test checks.

objectives.text: State a synonym and, where the sheet gives one, an antonym for each Lesson 1 word.
Recognize a word's synonym or antonym among other Lesson 1 vocabulary.

parentNote.text: Built from "Lesson 1 synonyms and antonyms.pdf," which says outright that the unit test draws from this list. The source is a 3-column table flattened by text extraction, and two words — jostle and pedestrian — come out with no antonym at all (checked twice, same result both times, so this reads as the sheet leaving them blank rather than a misread). Nothing is invented for those gaps: only their synonyms are tested. "Patient" carries synonyms for both of its senses — tolerant/composed as an adjective, victim/sufferer as the noun for someone under a doctor's care — and only the adjective sense had a antonym given, so that is the only one tested.

nextUp.text: The cards first, since a synonym only means something once the base word is solid — then the questions.

cards.def:
**Synonyms: adapt, adjust. Antonym: neglect, ignore.**
• If you're accustomed to a sound, you stop noticing it; if you neglect or ignore it, you never got used to it at all.

**Synonyms: attentive, watchful. Antonym: inattentive.**
• An alert lookout is attentive; an inattentive one misses what is right in front of them.

**Synonyms: set, give. Antonym: reject.**
• A teacher can assign extra credit, or a student can reject it and turn it down.

**Synonyms: stir, shift. Antonym: oppose.**
• A team that won't budge on a plan is refusing to shift; a team that opposes it is fighting it outright.

**Synonyms: sturdy, well-built. Antonym: slight.**
• A burly wrestler and a slight, narrow-framed gymnast are built in opposite ways.

**Synonyms: partner, friend. Antonym: foe.**
• A companion travels beside you; a foe works against you.

**Synonyms: together, cooperative. Antonym: disagreeable.**
• Compatible roommates get along easily; disagreeable ones argue over everything.

**Synonyms: idea, notion. Antonym: fact.**
• A concept is still just an idea being worked out; a fact has already been proven true.

**Synonyms: divert, sidetrack. Antonym: focus.**
• Noise in the hallway can distract you from homework; closing the door helps you focus instead.

**Synonyms: bump, knock, shove.**
• A crowded hallway is full of jostling — everyone bumping and knocking into everyone else.

**Synonyms: compliant, dutiful. Antonym: defiant.**
• An obedient dog sits the first time you ask; a defiant one plants its paws and refuses.

**Synonyms: barrier, hurdle. Antonym: advantage.**
• A locked gate is an obstacle in your way; a shortcut is an advantage that helps you along.

**Synonyms: tolerant, composed. Antonym: complains.**
• As an adjective, patient means willing to wait calmly — the opposite of someone who complains at every delay. Patient is also a noun: victim and sufferer are close synonyms for the person a doctor is treating.

**Synonyms: walker, hiker.**
• A pedestrian crosses at the light on foot, the way a walker or a hiker covers ground — no engine involved.

**Synonyms: quit, stop, turn in, call it a day. Antonym: rise, wake.**
• You retire to bed when you are tired and ready to stop for the night; you rise or wake once you are done sleeping.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of accustom (to get used to something)?
questions.hint: Think about what "accustom" means, then find its match.
steps: Accustom means to get used to something — you stop noticing it.
The opposite of getting used to something is failing to notice or care about it at all.
That is "ignore."

ex.tip: You can also say "neglect" — both mean never paying it any attention.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of alert (attentive, watchful)?
questions.hint: Think about what "alert" means, then find its match.
steps: Alert means watchful and paying close attention.
The opposite of paying attention is not paying attention.
That is "inattentive."

ex.tip: The prefix "in-" flips a word to its opposite — attentive becomes inattentive.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of assign (to give someone a job or task)?
questions.hint: Think about what "assign" means, then find its match.
steps: Assign means to hand someone a task or job.
The opposite of handing something to someone is refusing to accept it.
That is "reject."

ex.tip: A teacher assigns homework; a student cannot reject it, but the WORD reject is still its opposite.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of budge (to move or shift slightly)?
questions.hint: Think about what "budge" means, then find its match.
steps: Budge means to move or give way, even a little.
The opposite of giving way is standing firmly against something.
That is "oppose."

ex.tip: A stuck jar lid "won't budge"; someone who opposes a plan won't give an inch either.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of burly (big and strongly built)?
questions.hint: Think about what "burly" means, then find its match.
steps: Burly describes someone big and strongly built.
The opposite build is small and thin.
That is "slight."

ex.tip: A "slight" person has a light, narrow frame — the opposite of burly.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of companion (a friend who spends time with you)?
questions.hint: Think about what "companion" means, then find its match.
steps: A companion is a friend who is on your side.
The opposite of a friend is an enemy.
That is "foe."

ex.tip: "Foe" is an old, short word for enemy — still used in stories about rivals and battles.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of compatible (getting along well)?
questions.hint: Think about what "compatible" means, then find its match.
steps: Compatible things or people get along smoothly together.
The opposite is not getting along — arguing or clashing.
That is "disagreeable."

ex.tip: Disagreeable roommates fight about everything compatible ones would settle easily.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of concept (a general idea)?
questions.hint: Think about what "concept" means, then find its match.
steps: A concept is an idea still being worked out — it might be true or it might not.
The opposite of an unproven idea is something already known to be true.
That is "fact."

ex.tip: Scientists start with a concept and test it until it becomes an established fact.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of distract (to pull attention away)?
questions.hint: Think about what "distract" means, then find its match.
steps: Distract means to pull someone's attention away from what they are doing.
The opposite of pulling attention away is keeping it locked on one thing.
That is "focus."

ex.tip: Closing your door to focus is the direct opposite of letting noise distract you.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of obedient (doing what you are asked)?
questions.hint: Think about what "obedient" means, then find its match.
steps: Obedient means doing what you are asked or told to do.
The opposite is refusing to do what you are told.
That is "defiant."

ex.tip: A defiant dog plants its paws and will not budge — the exact opposite of an obedient one.

questions.q: Which word means the OPPOSITE of obstacle (something blocking your way)?
questions.hint: Think about what "obstacle" means, then find its match.
steps: An obstacle is something in your way that makes progress harder.
The opposite of something that slows you down is something that helps you along.
That is "advantage."

ex.tip: A locked gate is an obstacle; a spare key someone hands you is an advantage.

questions.q: As an ADJECTIVE, which word means the OPPOSITE of patient (tolerant, willing to wait)?
questions.hint: Think about what "patient" means, then find its match.
steps: As an adjective, patient means calm and willing to wait without a fuss.
The opposite of waiting calmly is not waiting calmly at all.
That describes someone who complains.

ex.tip: Someone stuck in a slow line either waits patiently, or complains the whole time — opposite responses to the same wait.

questions.q: Which words mean the OPPOSITE of retire (to go to bed / stop for the day)?
questions.hint: Think about what "retire" means, then find its match.
steps: Retire can mean to go to bed or stop working for the day.
The opposite of going to sleep is coming out of sleep.
That is "rise" or "wake."

ex.tip: You retire tired at night and rise or wake once you are done sleeping — a clean before-and-after pair.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as jostle (to push or shove)?
questions.hint: Think about what "jostle" means, then find its match.
steps: Jostle means to bump or push against someone, often in a crowd.
A close match for "bump against someone" is "shove."
So the synonym is "shove."

ex.tip: "Bump," "knock" and "shove" all describe the same kind of crowded jostling.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as pedestrian (a person traveling on foot)?
questions.hint: Think about what "pedestrian" means, then find its match.
steps: A pedestrian is someone traveling on foot, not by car or bike.
Someone traveling on foot is simply called a walker.
So the synonym is "walker."

ex.tip: A hiker is also a synonym — both describe covering ground on foot.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as companion (a friend who spends time with you)?
questions.hint: Think about what "companion" means, then find its match.
steps: A companion is someone who spends time with you or does things with you.
Another word for someone you team up with is "partner."
So the synonym is "partner."

ex.tip: A travel companion and a travel partner mean essentially the same thing.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as obstacle (something blocking your way)?
questions.hint: Think about what "obstacle" means, then find its match.
steps: An obstacle is something that blocks your path or progress.
A word that means the same kind of blocking thing is "barrier."
So the synonym is "barrier."

ex.tip: A fallen tree on a trail is both an obstacle and a barrier — same idea, two words.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as concept (a general idea)?
questions.hint: Think about what "concept" means, then find its match.
steps: A concept is a general idea or thought about something.
The plainest match for "a general idea" is simply "idea."
So the synonym is "idea."

ex.tip: "Notion" is another synonym — all three describe a thought still taking shape.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as retire (to stop for the day)?
questions.hint: Think about what "retire" means, then find its match.
steps: Retire can mean to stop working or stop for the day.
A plain word for stopping something is "quit."
So the synonym is "quit."

ex.tip: "Turn in" and "call it a day" are two more ways people say the same thing.
